title: Unpatched Critical LMCache Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code Remotely
key_facts: JFrog disclosed on 7 Oct 2026 the flaw CVE-2026-105192 in LMCache, open-source software that speeds up LLM servers such as vLLM; JFrog rated it 9.8 out of 10 for a server bound to a routable address.
The flaw affects LMCache from version 0.3.9 (Oct 2025) through 0.5.5, the latest stable release, and also the 0.5.6 release candidates and the development branch; no fixed version exists.
The multiprocess server listens only on the local machine by default; it is reachable when an operator starts it on a routable address, as LMCache's own example Kubernetes deployment does.

The ZeroMQ socket has no authentication; one message type is unpickled before its type is checked, so a crafted message can run code with the LMCache process's privileges, which are root on the official container images according to JFrog.
The flaw was found by Yuval Moravchick of JFrog's security research team.
LMCache has not published a security advisory, and JFrog's advisory gives no way for operators to tell whether a server was already attacked.
A GitHub user opened six other LMCache security reports on 6 Oct 2026; they rest on proof-of-concept claims, have no CVE and no maintainer confirmation.
quote_evidence: A single network message to that server can run commands as the user the LMCache process runs as.
LMCache has not published a security advisory for the flaw.
why_it_matters_hint: A critical unpatched flaw can let an attacker who reaches the server run commands; operators must keep the port local or on a trusted network.
notes: Article read in full (4,323 characters). The closing vendor line on AI agents in enterprises is advertising and is not used. Single firm's disclosure; no maintainer advisory.
